#summary Useage instructions

= Useage =

AmFast can encode and decode Python objects to AMF3 format.


= Encoding =
{{{
import amfast.encoder as encoder
byte_string = encoder.encode(value)
}}}

encode(...)
    Description:
    =============
    Encode a Python object in AMF3 format.
    
    Useage:
    ===========
    byte_string = encode(value, **kwargs)
    
    Optional keyword arguments:
    ============================
     * use_array_collections - bool - True to encode lists and tuples as ArrayCollections - Default = False
     * use_object_proxies - bool - True to encode dicts as ObjectProxys - Default = False
     * use_references - bool - True to encode multiply occuring objects as references - Default = True
     * use_legacy_xml - bool - True to encode XML as old XMLDocument instead of E4X - Default = False
     * include_private - bool - True to encode attributes starting with a underscore  - Default = False
     * get_class_def - function - Function that retrieves a ClassDef object used for customizing serialization of objects - Default = amfast.class_def.get_class_def_by_class Custom functions must have the signature: class_def = function(class_), where class_ is the class of the object being encoded and class_def is a ClassDef instance, or None if no ClassDef was found.

= Decoding =
{{{
import amfast.decoder as decoder
py_obj = decoder.decode(byte_string)
}}}

decode(...)
    Description:
    ============
    Decode an AMF3 stream to Python objects.
    
    Useage:
    ===========
    py_obj = decode(value, **kwargs)
    
    Optional keyword arguments:
    ============================
     * use_array_collections - bool - True to decode ArrayCollections to lists. - Default = False
     * use_object_proxies - bool - True to decode ObjectProxies to dicts. - Default = False
     * get_class_def - function - Function that retrieves a ClassDef object used for customizing 
        serialization of objects - Default = amfast.class_def.get_class_def_by_class
        Custom functions must have the signature: class_def = function(class_), where class_ is the class of the object being decoded and class_def is a ClassDef instance, or None if no ClassDef was found.
